message:
Command `python3 -c "
# Count platforms
platforms = [
    'X86 32', 'X86 64', 'ARM', 'THUMB', 'Arm-V8', 'THUMB+V8', 'Thumb-MClass',
    'ARM-64', 'MIPS-32 (Big-endian)', 'MIPS-32 (micro)', 'MIPS-64-EL', 'MIPS-32-EL',
    'MIPS-64 (Big-endian)', 'MIPS-32 | Micro (Big-endian)', 'PPC-64', 'Sparc',
    'SparcV9', 'SystemZ', 'XCore', 'MIPS-32R6 (Big-endian)', 'MIPS-32R6 (Micro+Big-endian)',
    'MIPS-32R6 (Little-endian)', 'MIPS-32R6 (Micro+Little-endian)', 'M68K',
    'M680X_M6809', 'EVM', 'MOS65XX', 'tms320c64x', 'WASM'
]
print(f'platforms_len = {len(platforms)}')
print(f'28 % {len(platforms)} = {28 % len(platforms)}')
print(f'Platform at index {28 % len(platforms)}: {platforms[28 % len(platforms)]}')
"` executed with exit code 0.

message.content: No crash. Let me think about this more carefully. The issue is that the fuzzer uses `Data[0] % platforms_len` to select the architecture. With 29 platforms (0-28), `28 % 29 = 28` which is WASM. But let me verify:
